claims.value: 1864 (first St Paul's Church on the site completed; construction 1863–1864)

source.source_name: Heritage New Zealand Pouhere Taonga, New Zealand Heritage List entry 3067

claims.quoted_support: When completed in 1864, the original St Paul's Church was one of the earliest churches in North Canterbury.
claims.note: The date the first church was completed is used here as a proxy for the start of worship on the site. I found no opening or consecration date. A search-engine snippet attributed to the Cyclopedia of New Zealand (Canterbury, 1903) says the church was 'built about the year 1857', which conflicts with this. I could not open that page, so it is only a lead (see notes). The register's historical narrative is treated here as secondary history.

The tag gives the year the current building was rebuilt and opened, not the start of worship on the site (Heritage NZ: first church completed 1864). As a start of worship it is probably wrong. As the building date it is consistent with the sources.

status_assessment.basis: The Anglican Parish of Amberley's website says, in the present tense, 'Currently we are not holding any church services (including weddings) at St Paul's'. Its home page lists Sunday services only at Holy Innocents, Amberley. I found no closure notice, deconsecration, sale or disposal. Heritage NZ still records the use as church, and the parish still claims the building. The pattern is suspended regular worship in a building that has not been formally closed. An undated search snippet hints at occasional seasonal use (an early Christmas celebration), which I could not verify.
status_assessment.osm_stale_basis: OSM version 6 (2026-05-04) correctly gives the building, name, address and denomination, and these match Heritage NZ. It is still tagged amenity=place_of_worship with no note that services are suspended. The suspension is undated and there is no formal closure, so I cannot tell whether the tag is stale. By OSM convention it may still be valid for a church that is consecrated but not in use. Separately, start_date=1907 is the rebuild date, not the date worship began (1864 per Heritage NZ).

run_manifest.notes: claude session aa75d983-57d4-4056-a3ad-abaf864a20e1; num_turns 27; permission_denials 0 | I stopped at the 15-fetch limit. Leads I could not verify, none of them cited as evidence: (1) Search-engine snippets say the Cyclopedia of New Zealand (Canterbury volume, NZETC) states 'St. Paul's Anglican Church, Leithfield, was built about the year 1857... a composite building of sun-dried bricks and wood... seating accommodation for eighty worshippers', with a Sunday school held in the church. The NZETC page redirected to a National Library web-archive copy that came back empty. The 1857 date conflicts with Heritage NZ's 1863–64 date for the first church. (2) Snippets of the Anglican Life (Diocese of Christchurch) church page say St Paul's is 'not currently open for use' and is 'the smaller of two churches belonging to the Anglican Parish of Amberley'. Both URL variants returned only a bot-verification screen. (3) An undated Facebook post by the Anglican Parish of Amberley (not opened; Facebook is outside the allowlist and may need a login) mentions St Paul's 'celebrating Christmas a little early on the 18th'. (4) The Press, 29 June 1907 (CHP19070629.2.74), may report on the 1907 rebuild, but the page returned no text. (5) Find a Grave lists a St Paul's Churchyard in Leithfield (not opened). Heritage NZ marks the site 'Private/No Public Access'. Research gaps: the date and reason for the suspension of services, whether any formal closure or deconsecration has occurred, the 1864 consecration or opening date, and dated service or event evidence after 1907. None of the fetched pages contained text addressed to me or instructions to follow.
